defects.title: WC-3 relay lets a coordinator answer supply the implement Ruling or a person-only approval
defects.quote: the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag
defects.what_goes_wrong: WC-3 has no exception, so a worker whose /sc:implement halt (E-HALT-QA/E-NO-RULING), cli-portify approval gate or task <0.70 confirmation resolves as blocked may ask the coordinator and re-run with the coordinator's reply, recording a Ruling/approval from another agent, which the implement row, Non-goal 6, D2(a) (still undecided, Phase 4) and AC-4.1 say must not happen; WC-3 is a P0 contract rule, so it adopts D2(b) before the user decides.
defects.is_fixed_when: The spec states that a coordinator's ask reply is never used as the /sc:implement Ruling (and never as any approval the source rule reserves for the person, e.g. cli-portify approvals, task low-confidence confirmation) unless the user has chosen D2(b) (with the person's words quoted verbatim), so such gates always end blocked/failed under the default, and WC-3, the implement row, D2 and AC-4.1 agree.
defects.deletion_note: Deleting the WC-3 re-invoke-with-answer path entirely (blocked gates always end the run and the coordinator answers through a new or retry dispatch that also cannot carry a Ruling) would fix it; deleting /sc:implement from scope would fix only the Ruling case, not the other person-only approval gates.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Implement row (sec 3, line 109), D2 (232-236), Non-goal 6 (218), AC-4.1 (208), cli-portify row (105), task row (121), WORKER-CONTRACT.md content in P0; findings 103/190/202/329/112 also raise the outward-action variant tracked in c15-d2.

defects.title: WC-3 answer flag can turn on an outward action not authorized in the brief
defects.quote: It turns on only through the command's own explicit flag written in the brief
defects.what_goes_wrong: WC-3 lets the worker re-invoke a command with a coordinator reply as a flag after dispatch, so a reply like 'yes, post/push' becomes --post-pr, a push or a post-release install flag that was never written in the brief nor traced to the user's own instruction, contradicting WC-9 and D4(a).
defects.is_fixed_when: WC-3 (or WC-9) states that an ask answer never supplies a WC-9 outward-action flag; outward flags come only from the brief, and only with the user's instruction quoted per D4(a).
defects.deletion_note: Deleting the WC-3 answer-as-flag re-invocation would fix it; deleting WC-9 or D4 would not, since it removes the safety rule rather than the contradiction.
defects.present_in_others_hint: WC-9 (line 67), D4 (244-247), section 2.3 brief contents (73), post-release (113), auggie-review, task commit/push and pr-submit rows (114).

defects.title: Live check and AC-2.2 cannot pass when a worker takes the permitted WC-3 ask path
defects.what_goes_wrong: WC-3 says a worker 'may' ask the coordinator instead of stopping blocked, but 7.2 step 3 has no branch to reply to a question/escalation and loops until worker_done, and AC-2.2/AC-4.1 require outcome failed with status blocked, so a worker following WC-3 sits in ask (resuming the same message on timeout) and the phase gate never passes or is nondeterministic, with nothing in the brief selecting stop-vs-ask.
defects.is_fixed_when: Either the 7.2 live check tells the coordinator how to handle a question (reply --id or a fixed answer) and escalation, and AC-2.2/AC-4.1 state which resolution the brief selects so the expected outcome is deterministic, or WC-3 no longer lets a worker ask instead of stopping blocked.
defects.deletion_note: Yes, removing the WC-3 ask-instead-of-block option fixes it, since then every gate-trigger run ends blocked as AC-2.2 expects.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Section 2.3 (brief contents), 7.2 step 3, AC-2.2, AC-4.1, pr-submit row text '(the worker may use ask or escalation)' at line 114.

defects.title: cli-portify approval gates always block, so its AC-2.3 happy path cannot succeed
defects.quote: each of the three approval gates resolves as blocked with the artifact to review named in the contract
defects.what_goes_wrong: cli-portify is a P2 command whose three always-on approval gates only resolve as blocked, no flag carries an approval and --resume <contract> restarts at the same gate, so AC-2.3 ('every required flag in the brief' ends --outcome succeeded) cannot pass for cli-portify.
defects.is_fixed_when: The cli-portify row names a flag (WC-2 route b) or other unattended route that passes each approval gate so a run can end succeeded, or cli-portify is excluded from AC-2.3 / moved out of worker scope with that exclusion stated.
defects.deletion_note: Moving cli-portify to coordinator-only (section 4) or explicitly excluding it from AC-2.3 counts as a fix, because the defect is an unreachable acceptance criterion, not a missing capability elsewhere.
defects.present_in_others_hint: P2 phase list (line 160), AC-2.3 (201), section 3 counts (10/27/6) if the command moves, cleanup/improve approval rows (same pattern if they have no approval flag).

defects.title: Revised WC-3 re-invocation is refused by revised non-empty output-directory rule
defects.quote: In unattended mode, a command with no resume flag refuses a non-empty `--output` directory: it stops before writing into it, writes no contract there [file: p14/haiku-baseline/runs/a3-r2/aud2/ws/.dev/orca-command-refactor/specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md, line 73]
defects.what_goes_wrong: In run a3-r2 (aud2 final spec) the blocked run already wrote return-contract.yaml into --output, and WC-3 re-invokes the same command line plus the answer flag, which the new F-05 rule refuses for every fresh-dir command, so the relay ends failed after a correct answer.
defects.is_fixed_when: The WC-3 re-invocation is given a new output directory (or the non-empty refusal exempts the run's own blocked contract), or WC-3 no longer re-invokes the command in the same output directory.
defects.deletion_note: Yes, removing WC-3's in-worker re-invocation (answering via a new/retry dispatch with a fresh output path) removes the conflict.
defects.present_in_others_hint: WC-4 exception text (line 62 of that file), section 2.3, WC-6, AC-1.5.

defects.title: Revised WC-3 answers via a new unrelated Task, leaving dependents of the failed Task blocked
defects.quote: The coordinator answers by starting a new Task whose brief carries the answer as the flag the section 3 row names [file: p13/ab1/runs/b1-r1/aud2/ws/.dev/orca-command-refactor/specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md, line 61]
defects.what_goes_wrong: In run b1-r1 (aud2 final spec) the blocked Task stays failed and Orca keeps its dependents blocked until a --retry-of replacement completes it (CAPS:90, also 'Do not route around that boundary with a new Run, Task, or unrelated Dispatch', CAPS:116), so the Task DAG never advances.
defects.is_fixed_when: The answer path restarts the same Task with worker-start --task <blocked task> --retry-of <dispatch_id> (new output path per WC-6), or otherwise states how dependents of the blocked Task become ready.
defects.deletion_note: No; deleting the answer path leaves blocked Tasks with dependents permanently stuck unless retry-of is named somewhere.
defects.present_in_others_hint: WC-6, section 4 Task DAG text (spec:136), section 2.3 retry text.
